description: This Java source file contains a set of unit tests for the EncryptedDocument class, which appears to handle encrypted file storage and retrieval, including metadata and content, in an Android environment. The tests cover various scenarios such as reading/writing metadata and content, handling large files, error conditions, and compatibility with different document states.

classes.name: EncryptedDocumentTest
classes.description: A JUnit test case class for testing the EncryptedDocument class functionalities such as reading/writing metadata and content, handling errors, and edge cases in an Android environment.

methods.name: setUp
methods.description: Initializes test environment, creating a temporary file for testing.

methods.name: tearDown
methods.description: Cleans up test environment by deleting all files in the app's file directory.

methods.name: testEmptyFile
methods.description: Tests behavior when reading metadata and content from an empty file, expecting IOExceptions.

methods.name: testNormalMetadataAndContents
methods.description: Tests writing and reading small byte-content with associated metadata.

methods.name: testGiantMetadataAndContents
methods.description: Tests handling of large (over 1MB) byte-content, ensuring the system correctly processes large data sizes.

methods.name: testMetadataAndContents
methods.description: Helper method used by the above tests to write and verify metadata and content.

methods.name: testNormalMetadataOnly
methods.description: Tests writing only metadata without content and verifies correct retrieval.

methods.name: testCopiedFile
methods.description: Tests that reading metadata with a different document id (based on the same file) results in a digest error.

methods.name: testBitTwiddle
methods.description: Tests detection of data corruption by manually modifying the file after writing metadata.

methods.name: testErrorAbortsWrite
methods.description: Simulates an error during content writing to verify that the original metadata remains unchanged and that exceptions are properly propagated.
